findings.message: `summarize` annotates `percentiles: Optional[Sequence[float]]`, but this import line never brings in `Sequence`. Python 3.14 defers annotations and hides it, yet the package declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"`; on 3.9-3.13 `import gauge.series` raises NameError: name 'Sequence' is not defined, so the whole CLI is unusable on the versions it claims to support. `typing.get_type_hints` fails here ev
findings.evidence: from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple
findings.patch_old: from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple
findings.patch_new: from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

findings.message: The median is written last, after the box edges, so whenever a quartile collapses onto the median the median glyph erases the box boundary. `box` on [0,0,0,0,10] with --ascii prints `|-------------------|`: no box and no median at all, and [0,100,100] prints `[===================|`, losing the closing bracket. A skewed series is legal input and the plot silently drops two of the five numbers it cl
findings.evidence: cells[pos_med] = median_char

findings.message: Bin labels format each edge to six significant digits, so several adjacent bins can print the same pair: [1e16, 1e16+2] with 5 bins renders three rows labelled `[1e+16, 1e+16)` and counts that look impossible. Printing an edge at full precision when the compact form repeats the previous edge would keep every row self-describing.
findings.evidence: labels.append(f"[{format_number(low)}, {format_number(high)}{closing}")
